page.layout: One page of running text, with the running head at the top. The top part is set in italic; below a small ornament the main text is in roman. No marginal notes. The catchword "vi," stands at the lower right.

p.i: cidus [?] fit ac quietus, qui spiritus in oculis Dei magnifica ac sumptuosa res est. Nam ad eum modum olim & sanctae illae mulieres sperantes in Deo, comebant sese, & subditae erant suis viris, quemadmodum Sara obedivit Abrahae, dominum illum appellans, cuius factae estis filiae, dum benefacitis, & non terremini ullo pavore.
Viri similiter cohabitent secundum scientiam, velut infirmiori vasi muliebri impartientes honorem, tanquam etiam coheredes gratiae vitae, ne interrumpantur preces vestrae.

main_text.p: 1 D. Petrus postquam tradita fide bona opera ceu fidei fructus & signa docere coepisset, & singulorum ordinum officia praescribere: nunc ostendit quid conjuges facere debeant. Quandoquidem multum bonae frugis in matrimonio est, si recte instítutum sit in timore Dei. Nam & calamitates variae, & scelera innumera oriuntur ex conjugio malo. Qui hactenus de operibus bonis ex pontificiorum parte scripserunt, vere bona opera neglexerunt, fictitia quaedam laudibus extulere. Nam monachismum, ceremoniarum studium, jejunia, stolida, & preculas superstitiosas laudavere: interim vera Christianorum officia neglexere prorsus. page.notes: Top line: "cidus" is at the start of the first line and may be a fragment; the reading is uncertain, hence [?]. "comebant" is read as printed and is doubtful. The italic "pavore" is followed by a printed dash-like mark, rendered as a full stop. A small printed ornament stands between the italic passage and "1 D. Petrus"; it is not text. A tiny mark "1" stands below the catchword at bottom centre; it is not transcribed as a signature because it is not clearly a gathering signature. Long s is plain s throughout; the hyphen in "fecun-dum", "il-la", "fer-vi" is a line-end hyphen and is kept in the words as printed.
